name: Clipboard read
plain: Android shows a toast on read; iOS 16 asks Allow Paste; reading the change count is silent.
meaning: Clipboards hold passwords, 2FA codes and crypto addresses. Both OSes added visible signals so silent reads stop.

android.prompt_ui: Android 12 shows a toast when another app's clip is read
android.revocation: No setting; keep sensitive text flagged
android.note: Foreground only since 10; toast on read since Android 12; sensitive flag hides content in previews (Android 13)

ios.persistence: Settings > Apps > Paste from Other Apps
ios.api_surface: iOS 14 paste banner; iOS 16 Allow Paste prompt; changeCount readable with no prompt
ios.note: Silent reads from other apps are now announced

limits.headline: Can see what you copied while the app is open, and you may get a notice
limits.user_action: You tap Paste, or the app checks your clipboard when it opens
can: Look at the text or link you last copied while the app is in front
Check whether the clipboard changed, silently, on iPhone
Auto fill a copied code or link into a field
cannot: See the clipboard while the app is in the background (Android 10 and newer)
Do it unnoticed: Android 12 and newer shows a toast, and iOS 16 and newer asks Allow Paste
Show hidden contents in previews when the copied item is marked sensitive (Android 13)
See copies from other apps on iPhone without your Allow Paste choice
limits.reach_label: What you last copied, while open
limits.differs: Android shows a small toast. iPhone asks Allow Paste from iOS 16, though a paste button skips the prompt. The change counter can be checked without any prompt.

story.what_it_is: An app reads what you last copied, and the phone may or may not tell you.

marketing.name: Paste permission alert
marketing.pitch: iOS 16 asks before an app reads what you copied from another app, to protect your privacy.

marketing.name: Clipboard access toast
marketing.pitch: Android 12 shows a short message when an app reads the clipboard.

story.for_you: You copy a code, a password or a link, and any app may peek at it. Today you may see a small message when an app does. Reading only the change count, which tells an app that something new was copied, stays invisible.
story.for_makers: Makers use paste to fill a code or link and make flows smooth. Bad actors have used it to grab crypto addresses and passwords. Platforms added alerts after many apps were caught reading it on launch.

use_cases.example: A chat app sees a copied invite link and offers to open the group straight away.
A bank app fills in a one time code you just copied from a text message.
A shopping app spots a copied product link and offers to show the price.
A game notices a copied friend code and adds the friend in one tap.
A malicious app swaps a copied crypto wallet address for the thief's address.
An ad SDK reads the copied text to learn what you are interested in, which regulators call abuse.

story.android_note: Android 12 and later show a toast when another app reads your clipboard, but there is no prompt to block it.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows an Allow Paste prompt for paste from other apps, and apps can read the change count without a prompt.

technical_bounds: Can only be read while foregrounded

linkedin.how: July 2020: iOS 14 beta banners showed LinkedIn's iPhone and iPad apps reading the clipboard after each keystroke. VP Engineering Erran Berger said the app only compared clipboard text with the typed text, stored and sent nothing, and a fix was submitted. Bauer v. LinkedIn (N.D. Cal., 5:20-cv-04599) was filed 10 July 2020; outcome unverified.
